text:
Jules R: Hey folks, new hire day 3. Trying to set up a kubeconfig that only contains the dev cluster/context and my user. My current ~/.kube/config is an unreadable mess. What's the clean, recommended way to export a single-context kubeconfig? Also curious: for local tools (K9s, Lens) is it better to use a serviceaccount token or my SSO user creds?

Tara V: Welcome Jules :wave: Quickest way: switch to the desired context then run `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > ~/.kube/config.dev` and set `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config.dev` in your shell or add to your tool. That gives you a single-context file.

Jules R: Nice, thanks. I tried that but my SA token route hit a snag: `kubectl -n dev get sa/jules-sa -o yaml` shows no secret and automountServiceAccountToken: false. I don't want to change that cluster-wide. What's the modern best practice to get a short-lived token for a SA?

Platform Team: We prefer TokenRequest (projected tokens) over creating long-lived secrets. If your cluster supports it, `kubectl -n dev create token jules-sa --duration=2h` is the easiest. That uses the TokenRequest API and returns a token you can paste into kubeconfig. If your cluster is older, open an INF ticket and infra can create a temporary secret for you.

Jules R: The cluster is EKS but older; `kubectl create token` errors with unknown command. Ugh.

Platform Team: For older EKS versions, infra can mint a short-lived kubeconfig and give you a flattened file. We discourage manual SA secret creation. For Lens/K9s we advise using your SSO user credentials via the exec plugin (aws/gcloud) when possible. Use SA tokens only for CI or tightly-scoped local debugging.

Jules R: Got it. One more: I sometimes need to port-forward and debug pods; infra doc suggests a namespaced Role with pods/portforward. Is that safe for devs?

Tara V: Yes, that's the typical pattern. Role in the namespace granting `create` on `pods/portforward` + `get` is fine. Ask infra to apply a timeboxed RoleBinding bound to your user if you need it for >1 hour. Avoid cluster-level bindings.

infra-bot: Reminder: do not request cluster-admin. For temporary namespace-scoped elevation open INF with exact verbs, resources, and duration. All grants are logged and auto-revoked if timeboxed.

Jules R: Perfect, filing INF-1991 requesting a 2-hour RoleBinding for port-forwarding and a flattened kubeconfig for the dev cluster. Thanks all, this cleared things up!
